name: Ellen Baran
life: “I left machine work for the railroad when the cold started to hurt my fingers.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Ellen by a small Friday habit. Ellen looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I store nuts in my tin. Finding somebody else's lunch inside made me remember to eat.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Ellen has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Ellen presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Ellen enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To bring something edible to the next railway break.
family: Jo Emery is Ellen’s cousin raised in the same household. Ellen checks the date twice. Jo brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Jo says, “I cannot fund another hour. I offered a place to wait for children whose parents are out with the car.”
connections: Joanna Ellis. They arrange a lunchtime domino rematch with actual food in the tins.
